attempted_claim: Let K be a hyperbolic two-bridge knot with crossing number 12 to 16 inclusive and let A_K(M,L) be its SL(2,C) A-polynomial with Newton-polygon edge-slope set S(N) in standard Dehn-surgery coordinates. Question: does there exist such a K admitting an exceptional Dehn filling at an integral or half-integral slope e (meaning K(e) is reducible, toroidal, or small Seifert-fibered) such that e is at distance at least 1 from every slope in S(N)? A complete answer names K by Schubert fraction and knot table/Dowker-Thistlethwaite identifier, certifies the crossing number and hyperbolicity, computes A_K and its Newton edge slopes, identifies the witness slope e with a rigorous classification of K(e) into one of the three exceptional types (including the Seifert invariants or torus/reducing data), and verifies the distance inequality against S(N), or else for one explicitly named K certifies its full Brittenham-Wu exceptional-surgery list and its S(N) and shows every exceptional slope lies within distance <1 of S(N).
decisive_failure: No certified A-polynomial, Newton edge-slope set, hyperbolicity certificate, or full exceptional-surgery list was established for any 12-16-crossing two-bridge knot; Sage-gated exact SnapPy and Spherogram methods were unavailable and controlled literature retrieval failed, so neither target disjunct could be rigorously closed within the pass.
